editorial:
Imagine being the leader of a massive country but having no idea how to actually run it. That is exactly where you find yourself when you dive into this story. You get to see the inner circle of the Russian royal family, from the soft-hearted Tsar Nicholas II to his kids. The movie feels like a giant, slow-motion car crash. You watch as they ignore the starving people outside their palace walls, trusting the wrong advisors and clinging to a way of life that is already dead. It is a heavy watch, but it does a great job of showing how a few bad decisions can ruin everything for a whole family.

The acting is top-notch and makes you feel bad for people who weren't exactly saints. While the middle part drags a bit, the way the tension builds up to the revolution is great. If you love history or stories about fallen empires, you will really dig this. Since it is an older film, you should try to find a high-quality version to keep the costumes looking sharp. I would suggest adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best colors, or just renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The movie ends in a very sad way. After being moved from one prison to another, the royal family is taken into a dark basement in the middle of the night. The Bolshevik soldiers open fire on them, killing the Tsar, his wife, and all their children. There is no big escape or happy twist. It wraps up by showing that the old world of kings is gone and a new, violent era has started.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and royal family tragedies.
